# UQDA Core v0.1.1

This security and packaging update supersedes v0.1.0.

## Security

- Requires Go 1.25.13 or newer. The v0.1.0 binaries were built with Go 1.25.0,
  for which a current `govulncheck` scan reports 27 reachable standard-library
  vulnerabilities. The same scan reports zero reachable vulnerabilities after
  rebuilding with Go 1.25.13.
- Retains the hardened authenticated handshake and root-only local
  administration socket introduced before the stable release.
- Publishes signed SHA-256 manifests and GitHub artifact attestations for every
  release asset.
- Fixes a data race between Ironwood peer RTT updates and peer-status snapshots.
- Derives group authentication secrets with Argon2id instead of fast SHA-256,
  making offline password guessing substantially more expensive. Nodes that
  configure `GroupPassword` must upgrade together; v0.1.0 group-password nodes
  cannot authenticate v0.1.1 nodes.

## macOS notice

UQDA does not currently have a paid Apple Developer account. The macOS assets
are therefore explicitly named `*-unsigned.pkg` and Finder will display a
Gatekeeper warning. This warning means Apple has not signed and notarized the
package; it is not a malware scan result.

Prefer the release `install.sh` path. It discovers the correct macOS package,
verifies its SHA-256 digest against this release's signed manifest, and then
invokes the system installer. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally. The release
workflow is ready to sign and notarize automatically if Apple credentials are
configured in the future.

## Validation

- Linux, Windows and macOS builds and unit tests with patched Go 1.25 and Go
  1.26;
- FreeBSD and OpenBSD cross-builds;
- five privileged Linux mesh scenarios covering two-node transport, multi-hop
  routing, failover, loss/latency and secure-required compatibility;
- race detection, handshake fuzzing, CodeQL, linting and reachable dependency
  vulnerability scanning;
- native package builds for supported Debian, macOS, Windows, EdgeOS and VyOS
  targets.

## Future releases

Stable publishing is now driven by a versioned file in `.github/releases/`.
Adding the newest stable SemVer notes file and merging its fully tested pull
request runs the complete build, signing, attestation, and publication pipeline
without another hard-coded version setting. Version resolution is explicitly
run through Bash on every runner so Linux, macOS, and Windows use the same path.
